text:
elaine: Heads up — ran a perf sweep on the 8xA100 multi-node config and hit a weird regression when jobs cross node boundary (NVLink local -> EFA cross-node). baseline local: ~18ms per 1k tokens; cross-node: ~34-42ms and big variance.

omar: ouch. same job/seq len/batch?

elaine: same model shard layout, same batcher. changed only network: single-node NVLink vs two-node EFA fabric. profiling shows allreduce spikes and kernel selector falling back to a generic matmul kernel at certain seq lengths.

jin: can you paste the microprof output?

elaine: sure — snip from perf run:
```
allreduce: mean 0.84ms (NVLink), 3.9ms (EFA) for 512KB payloads
nccl: using ring, comms_wait spikes ~3.2ms
kernel_selector: selected optimized_fused_attn for seq<=1024, fallback to generic_attn for seq>1024 on device 3
kvcache: prefetch shards causing extra allreduce of offsets
```

tess: fallback kernel sounds suspicious — why would kernel selection change across nodes? that should be deterministic by shape + hw.

elaine: we think it's shape-inferred + batching heuristics. when EFA introduced higher comm latency, the runtime increased batch packing to keep GPU utilization, which bumped effective seq for some microbatches >1024 and triggered different kernel path.

mike: so it's a feedback loop: slower network -> larger GPU queues -> different batching -> kernel fallback -> slower compute -> more queuing -> more comm pressure.

peter: classic. can we force the optimized kernel to run to isolate?

elaine: I forced KERNEL_FORCE=optimized_fused_attn on one run: compute latency dropped ~12%, but total end-to-end still worse than NVLink because allreduce dominates.

omar: do we have NCCL topo / ring vs tree differences across EFA? maybe ring is terrible at these sizes. try enabling NCCL_TREE or hierarchical algos.

jin: also check gpudirect rdma setting. if RDMA not used, bandwidth collapses. infra-bot: note — EFA clusters have GPUDirect enabled in region staging-2.

infra-bot: @eng-runtime FYI — staging-2 EFA nodes currently have gpudirect=enabled, mtu=9000.

tess: can we add per-token allreduce profiling in the runtime? 1) record payload size per-step, 2) record algorithm chosen by NCCL. then correlate with kernel selection and batch size.

elaine: I already logged per-step sizes. attaching a short excerpt (trimmed):
```
step 120: kv_payload 480KB, allreduce 3.6ms, kernel=optimized_fused_attn
step 121: kv_payload 768KB, allreduce 4.1ms, kernel=generic_attn
step 122: kv_payload 512KB, allreduce 3.9ms, kernel=generic_attn
```

mike: interesting that optimized_fused_attn still appears at smaller payloads. maybe kernel threshold ties to peak sequence in the batch not avg.

omar: for a quick experiment: 1) pin batcher to max_seq cap 1024 (no dynamic packing) 2) force NCCL_ALGO=tree 3) run allreduce microbench (ib_send_lat or nccl-tests) across nodes. can someone run nccl-tests?

peter: I'll run nccl-tests tonight across 2 nodes and post results.

jin: also worth trying async allreduce overlap mode: start reduce as soon as KV shards ready rather than waiting for full step to finish. could hide latency.

elaine: tried async overlap in canary — improvements ~8-10% on EFA but still behind NVLink by 1.5x.

tess: maybe the KV sharding scheme causes duplication of offsets or extra metadata allreduces across nodes. check if we broadcast keys or reduce them.

elaine: good call — found an extra hull-reduce of 64B metadata every step that scales with world_size. cheap per-step but high-rate. removed in a branch and perf improved ~4%.

mike: small wins add up. also consider quantizing distributed comms (compress gradients/kv) for large payloads. but that's more invasive.

omar: infra question — is EFA path going through PCIe->NIC or via GPUDirect? if it falls back to staging path we see copies.

infra-bot: confirmed gpudirect active; no HOST fallback observed in NIC logs during test window.

peter: nccl-tests (ring) results: bandwidth ~40GB/s NVLink local, ~18GB/s EFA across nodes for our message sizes. latency: 0.2ms NVLink vs 1.7ms EFA (512KB). posting raw next message.

elaine: thanks. given this, we should:
- add topology-aware scheduler that keeps shards local when possible (prefer intra-node grouping)
- cap dynamic packing to avoid kernel-path changes
- add per-step comm algorithm telemetry (nccl algorithm + payload)
- investigate hierarchical allreduce (node-local then inter-node)

tess: agree. propose RFC for runtime changes, include benchmarks and a new metric: comm/compute overlap ratio.

mike: I'll prototype a node-aware placement policy that prefers full-shard locality and falls back to cross-node only if necessary.

omar: also add unit test that replays the failing trace with deterministic network injection (delay) so we don't regress again.

elaine: created a reproducer gist and pinned logs to the thread. thanks all. :raised_hands:

peter: :eyes: will share nccl-tests output soon.

jin: moving to action items — I'll open tickets for kernel-threshold caps and per-step telemetry.

infra-bot: ticket created: INFRA-4821 (EFA perf tests)

elaine: closing loop — goal is parity within 20% of NVLink for our common workloads. will iterate.
